text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Low-fat diet cuts breast-cancer risk: Nutrition experiment produces significant reduction in risk-raising dense tissue.
- Ontario lists top earners on payroll: Nearly 5,000 make C$100,000 or more.
- Rock sees end to Pearson lawsuit: Authority says sale not linked to suit.
- For those on top, crisis changes little: The country may be falling apart but life goes on as usual for political class.
- Interest rates rise as dollar takes beating.
- Bre-X geologist beset by troubles: De Guzman 'happy' on last day of life.
- Dollar, bond market plunge: Banks raise mortgage rates as currency nears lowest level in two years in volatile session.
- Bre-X delays report, hit with 3 more suits: Trading frenzy overloads computers at Toronto, Montreal exchanges.
- Latest TSE computer crash angers investors, members: Exchange shut for 45 minutes as volume soars.
- Fun with Statscan figures: A different take on the job market by two surveys has fired up political junkies and created a mini media dustup over 'voodoo arithmetic.'
- Ontario Hydro denied greater U.S. access: FERC wants end to utility's monopoly.
- Pressure builds for higher rates: Mortgage rates jump, C$ falls to two-year low and the market bets Bank of Canada will tighten credit.
- Bre-X frenzy pushes shares higher again.
